A rating's uncertainty, source by source

Source: R/rating_uncertainty.R
rating_uncertainty.Rd

A rating's uncertainty has several sources, and they behave differently. rating_uncertainty() reports each on its own and the combination, so a reviewer can see what a band is made of:

  • Sampling. The rating would differ with a different set of gaugings. Each draw resamples the gaugings used, with replacement, and refits with the rating's own settings and breakpoints. Random error in each gauging is part of this source already: it is the scatter of the gaugings about the curve, and resampling carries it into the band.

  • Gauging. Error shared between gaugings: a current meter, a method or a team reading high or low for all of them. It leaves no scatter, so sampling cannot see it. Each draw moves the discharge of every gauging in a group by one shared factor, exp(e) with e ~ Normal(0, u^2). With group_by, each group (a method, a meter) has its own draw; without, every gauging shares one.

  • Combined. Each draw resamples, then applies the shared error, then refits. The two sources are taken as independent, and are never added.

  • Structure. Another reasonable choice would give another curve: the other objective, a limb fewer (each breakpoint dropped), a breakpoint moved. Reported as a range (the lowest and highest curve, with the variant giving each), never as an interval: structure has no probability, only a spread of defensible choices.

The package does not invent u. It comes from the evidence's optional discharge_uncertainty column (a fraction per gauging; a group's value is the median of its gaugings') or, failing that, from gauging_uncertainty. With neither, the gauging and combined sources are reported as not assessed, with the reason. They are never reported as zero.

With one group and no magnitude protection set in discharge, a shared factor k on every discharge scales the fitted C by exactly k and leaves a and n as they were, under either objective, so the gauging draws need no refit: the curve is multiplied by k. With groups, or with protect_above, every draw is refitted.

The method, its failure behaviour and its limitations are set out in design/E2_separated_uncertainty.md.

Usage

rating_uncertainty(
  rating,
  stage = NULL,
  n_draws = 500,
  gauging_uncertainty = NULL,
  group_by = NULL,
  sources = c("sampling", "gauging", "structure"),
  level = 0.95,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

rating

A FlodeRating or FlodeSegmentedRating fitted from evidence. A FlodeRatingTable holds no evidence to resample and is refused.

stage

Stages to report at, metres. Default: 50 stages over the gauged range.

n_draws

Draws per resampling source, 100 or more. Default 500.

gauging_uncertainty

One fraction for all gaugings, such as 0.05, in (0, 0.5], used where the evidence has no discharge_uncertainty.

group_by

Optional: the name of an evidence column (such as the method or the meter). Gaugings sharing a value share an error; groups are independent.

sources

Which of "sampling", "gauging" and "structure" to assess. "combined" is reported whenever sampling and gauging both are.

level

Width of the intervals. Default 0.95.

seed

Integer or NULL, recorded.

Value

A FlodeUncertainty.

See also

FlodeUncertainty, uncertainty_bands(), rating_sensitivity()

Examples

set.seed(1)
stage_m <- sort(runif(25, 0.3, 3))
gaugings <- data.frame(stage_m = stage_m,
                       discharge_cms = 3 * (stage_m - 0.1)^1.6 * exp(rnorm(25, sd = 0.05)))
fit <- fit_rating(gaugings, quiet = TRUE)
u <- rating_uncertainty(fit, n_draws = 100, gauging_uncertainty = 0.03, seed = 1)
u
#> <FlodeUncertainty> 95% intervals, 100 draws per resampling source
#>   sampling:  -10.4% to +10.3% of the rating, widest, over the gauged range
#>   gauging:   -5.6% to +6.1% of the rating, widest, over the gauged range
#>   combined:  -9.5% to +8.7% of the rating, widest, over the gauged range
#>   structure: range -1.1% to +12.7% of the rating over the gauged range (1 variant(s); a range, not an interval)
#>   Not a complete budget: stage error is not modelled.
head(uncertainty_bands(u))
